name: surface_ids
description: The closed set of surface types in the world, and the number each one is known by. Every consumer of a surface agrees on these numbers: the surface-ID map's R8 texels, a prop's `surface:<id>` tag in its GLB extras, and surface_fx_table.json. An id is a contract, so ids are never reused and never renumbered — a retired surface keeps its number and gains `retired: true`.

encoding.map: terrain_surface_id_map, lossless R8, 1025x1025 over the 1 km terrain (about 0.98 m per texel)
encoding.glb_extra: surface:<id>, an integer in the GLB extras of a prop or building
encoding.lookup: surface_fx_table.json, keyed by the same ids
encoding.why_r8_and_not_a_palette: An 8-bit index is lossless and exactly representable; a colour palette would be lossy after sRGB conversion and would need its own lookup anyway. 255 usable ids is more than this world will ever have surfaces.
encoding.why_1025: A 1024-cell terrain needs 1025 height samples, and this map shares that grid so a texel centre lands on a height sample rather than half a texel away from one. Every terrain map — heightmap, biome, surface ids, hydrology, splats — is 1025x1025 for that reason. An earlier version of this file said 1024x1024, which contradicted every generator.

reserved.0: unknown — a texel no generator has claimed. Treated as `dirt_path` for audio and VFX so a gap is quiet rather than silent, but it is a defect and the validator reports how many texels use it.
reserved.255: out of bounds — outside the terrain. Never audible, never stepped on.

surfaces.name: mud
surfaces.note: the bog basin floor; boots sink and the step is heavy

surfaces.name: water_shallow
surfaces.note: drawn by the water shader, not by the opaque material system, so it has no material row

surfaces.name: ash
surfaces.note: burned settlement ground; deliberately not snow

wetness_kinds.soaks: darkens strongly and stays dark: wetness_darken at the high end of its range
wetness_kinds.beads: darkens little and gains a specular sheen: low wetness_darken, roughness driven down hard
wetness_kinds.always_wet: ignores global_wetness; the surface is water

rules: An id is assigned once. Removing a surface sets retired: true and keeps the number.
A new surface takes the next unused id; ids are not chosen for their order in this file.
The map, the GLB extras and surface_fx_table.json must all cover every non-retired id, and tools/validate/check_materials.py enforces that.
